container.named_volumes: silently has no effect on apple-container (podman named volumes (no equivalent on apple-container)). See issue #120 for the parity plan.
container.podman_secrets: silently has no effect on apple-container (Podman secret refs (no host Podman secret store on apple-container; use cage.yaml `secret_injection:` or env: instead)). See issue #120 for the parity plan.
container.ports: silently has no effect on apple-container (inbound published ports — Apple's runtime has no host port-publishing (no `--publish`); reach the cage by its vmnet IP instead). See issue #120 for the parity plan.
container.userns: silently has no effect on apple-container (user namespace remap (the supervisor drops to a fixed uid 1000 — no remap layer)). See issue #120 for the parity plan.
container.drop_capabilities: silently has no effect on apple-container (custom drop list — the supervisor unconditionally drops ALL caps; your selective drop list has no effect). See issue #120 for the parity plan.
container.read_only: silently has no effect on apple-container (read-only rootfs — apple-container's rootfs is always RW, so `read_only: true` cannot be enforced). See issue #120 for the parity plan.
container.security_label_disable: silently has no effect on apple-container (SELinux label control — apple-container's microVM has no SELinux). See issue #120 for the parity plan.
container.tmpfs: the mounts ARE applied on apple-container, but their OPTIONS are not — Apple's `container run --tmpfs` takes a bare path, so /tmp, /workspace/.git/hooks, /workspace/.claude get kernel-default tmpfs semantics: noexec/nosuid/nodev are NOT enforced and any `size=` cap is ignored (an unbounded tmpfs can exhaust the cage VM's memory; bound it with container.memory). The mask entries (/workspace/.git/hooks, /workspace/.claude) do still block their cage→host / cage→cage pivot: that protection comes from the tmpfs overlaying the bind, not from `noexec`. See #120.
